title: SK hynix projects AI infrastructure performance to grow 20-fold by 2030
key_facts: SK hynix projected on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 that the performance scale of AI infrastructure will grow roughly 20-fold by 2030, driven by demand for AI inference.
Ahn Hyun, head of development at SK hynix, made the projection in a keynote at the 2026 Semiconductor Exhibition (SEDEX), which opened that day for three days in southern Seoul.
Ahn said inference demand is expanding in three areas at once: task complexity, the amount of information processed at a time, and the volume of requests.
Memory is becoming more important for storing and moving data; growing key-value (KV) cache needs require data to be spread across HBM, DRAM and SSDs.
SK hynix is pursuing 3D stacked DRAM and high-bandwidth flash (HBF) while improving its current HBM products.
quote_evidence: SK hynix Inc. projected Wednesday that the performance scale of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure will grow roughly 20-fold by 2030, driven by rapidly rising demand for AI inference.

Ahn Hyun, head of development at the South Korean chip giant, made the projection during his keynote speech at the 2026 Semiconductor Exhibition (SEDEX), which opened earlier in the day for a three-day run in southern Seoul.

SK hynix is pursuing next-generation memory technologies, including 3D stacked DRAM and high-bandwidth flash (HBF), while continuing to enhance the performance of existing HBM products, the executive added.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading memory maker expects memory demand to keep rising with AI inference.
notes: Company projection from a keynote; Yonhap does not say what 'performance scale' measures or give a method.
